findings.claim: The analysis omits evaluation of the required liter-llm model routing dependency and instead treats model-policy mapping as build-required without assessing the existing local candidate.
findings.evidence: Goals require "model strength/cost/capability routing via liter-llm" and the file tree contains "./tools/liter-llm", but library-candidates.json has no candidate for liter-llm; its build_required entry says "Native adapter coverage and model-policy mapping" with "why_no_candidate": "Common config cannot replace native-specific schemas and capability diagnostics."
findings.suggested_fix: Add liter-llm as a candidate, inspect its local contract/version/maintenance status, and state whether to adapt it for model capability/cost routing or why it is unsuitable.

findings.claim: The analysis does not provide a strategy or candidate evaluation for the required Docusaurus site updates, so the plan can omit a stated delivery surface.
findings.evidence: Goals require "update skills, agents, plugins, marketplaces, repository docs and both Docusaurus sites"; analysis.md discusses "Regenerate owned surfaces" and "repository docs" but never mentions Docusaurus or site update mechanics, and library-candidates.json gaps are only "process-conflicts", "team-runtime", "native-fidelity", "memory-models", and "packaging".
findings.suggested_fix: Add a documentation/site gap covering both Docusaurus sites, identify existing site build/update mechanisms in each repository, and define validation expected for those site changes.
